asr.engine: pocketsphinx 5.1.1 (bundled US-English model and CMU dictionary)
asr.purpose: offline sanity check of the words only; it cannot judge acting or naturalness
asr.rule: a take is 'intelligible' if free decoding gets every word (WER 0) or, decoding against a grammar of all 385 lines, it picks its own line
asr.diagnosis_rule:
For a take the recognizer could not confirm, every decode below uses a recognizer built for that one
    utterance. (1) The take itself: if a fresh recognizer confirms it, the miss was the shared recognizer's
    adaptation. (2) The same words read plainly (no performance DSP, no pitch shift; same sentence split, edges and
    level as a take) by the role's OWN voice, and by two reference voices (af_heart, am_michael). (3) For a
    pitch-shifted role, the take shifted back. Verdicts: the own voice fails too -> the recognizer does not
    follow this voice on these words (not the processing); the shifted-back take passes -> the role pitch; the own
    voice passes but the take does not -> the performance processing made it harder: LISTEN; nothing passes ->
    a limit of the recognizer.
why_free_wer_is_high_on_some_lines: 1-3 word lines ('Attack.', 'Down!', 'Mostly.') give the language model no context.
British voices (narrator, king, guard captain, musician, old woman...) against a US-English recognizer (measured in the preview: British voices WER 0.53-0.65 vs American 0.06-0.12 on the same line).
Names and rare words (Verdor, Scrapper, gawping) are not in the recognizer's language model; whispered and processed lines (whisper, pain, shout) are harder for it by design.
